sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth was front-loaded: revenue rose 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then slowed to 0.1% in FY2023 before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 loss of $3,445.1 million was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation, primarily the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F32][P74].
The operating loss narrowed from $3,485.6 million in FY2017 to $532.2 million in FY2025, lifting operating margin from -422.5% to -9.0% [F12][F20][F22][F30].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth, while Rest of world contributed 3.7pp [D456][D458][D499][D406].

FY2025 advertising revenue rose $282.4 million on roughly 17% more impressions, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression, and other revenue rose $287.6 million on subscription growth [P24].
Other revenue reached 12.6% of revenue in FY2025 and contributed 5.4pp of growth, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp [D543][D545][D538].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so revenue growth exceeded operating-cost growth by 5.5pp [D423][D406][D430].
The loss per diluted share narrowed 35.7% in FY2025 against a 34.0% smaller net loss, as the diluted share count rose 2.1% [D410][D408][D425].
FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a median of -32.4% and a low of -422.5% in FY2017 [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The 5.7pp operating-margin gain in FY2025 came from cost of revenue (+1.1pp), R&D (+1.3pp) and other lines (+3.3pp) [D419][D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, while R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P22][P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin, helped by $68.9 million of other income that included $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains [F50][F30][X130][P18].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million in FY2025 exceeded the $460.5 million net loss, and free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin and the window high [F80][F40][F100][D393][D560].
Operating cash flow rose from $413.5 million in FY2024 on non-cash stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and a $45.9 million increase in accounts payable [F79][F80][P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A of $163.6 million [F90][D392][D395][X80].
Capex in both years was primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Net cash swung from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, or -10.1% of revenue [D211][D399][D400].
That net-cash ratio ranks at the 0th percentile of five internet peers, whose median is 45.0% of revenue [D578][D579].
Liquidity remains ample: cash and investments of $2,940.6 million against total debt of $3,536.8 million, with a current ratio of 3.56x [D397][D398][F180].
In February 2025 the company issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of notes, producing a $66.9 million gain on extinguishment [P2][P1].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow in FY2025, while the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D401][D402][D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing, but ten straight loss years leave no demonstrated ability to earn a profit through a downturn [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390].
At 191.1% of the FY2025 operating loss, stock compensation is the main reason the GAAP loss persists while cash flow turns positive [D404].
Net cash fell for four straight years into net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, and buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R3][R4][D399][D307][D354][D402].
Funding repurchases above free cash flow while the balance sheet is in net debt is the capital-allocation risk to watch [R4].
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the FY2025 -9.0% level, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30].
Whether free cash flow margin stays above the FY2025 7.4% high, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D393].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue recovers from the FY2025 -10.1%, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D400].
